defect.old_behavior: The detector was evaluated over both model-visible chat spans and metadata-provided authority spans. A detector-only method could therefore consume the provenance annotation whose absence it was intended to model.
defect.detection: The final cross-run equivalence audit found that detector-only and 100% provenance-drop conditions had different excluded-token sets despite targeting the same remaining detector signal.
defect.impact: Detector-only pilot and full controls are invalid for identifiability claims. Hybrid provenance-drop and boundary-shrink cells remain valid because any detector tokens from a retained metadata span are a subset of the provenance-excluded span, while dropped spans leave the independently localized chat detector unchanged. Main base-versus-Authority runs are also unchanged for the same set-union reason.

resolution.detector_signal: Compute detector exclusions exclusively from source=chat_message spans.
resolution.provenance_signal: Continue computing typed provenance exclusions from metadata/inferred spans independently.
resolution.hybrid_signal: Use the union of the independent chat detector and provenance sets.
required_reruns: Streaming detector-only full run on 300 messages.

preserved_runs.main_external_fullscale: All four final full-scale base-versus-Authority runs.
preserved_runs.hybrid_robustness: All provenance-drop and boundary-shrink pilot/full cells.

acceptance: A unit test proves detector-only exclusions omit metadata_marker tokens.
The hybrid method still contains both independent chat-detector and provenance tokens.
Corrected detector-only runs have exact expected row counts and zero errors.
Corrected detector-only and 100% provenance-drop Streaming runs have identical excluded-token sets and generated outputs.
All execution and label-isolation audits pass.
